handoff.objective: Settle how much of ANOM-3 survives, using the checks the BATCH-011 reviews named and left unrun. ANOM-3: under RC.MATZOV, estimator.lwe_dual.matzov costs 139.66/196.37/262.34 against primal_bdd's 140.20/200.96/270.72 and NIST cutoffs 143/207/272. Its security reading is already dissolved twice (shared independence law; EV-MLKEM-020 memory charging). What is open is whether the INTERNAL comparison is a finding or an artifact, and whether the load-bearing 768/1024 numbers are trustworthy on an instrument path no Sage reference covers.
handoff.uncertainty_reduced: Whether the 768/1024 figures rest on anything checkable, and whether the matzov-beats-primal_bdd ordering survives the mutations that should destroy it if it is an artifact.
constraints: Never fabricate a command, output, timing, statistic, citation, or run (AGENTS.md rule 9).
Run the known-answer control FIRST as step 0 on the COMMITTED shim with no patch, and abort on non-zero exit. Record its output verbatim.

S1 SAGE REFERENCE, the check the red team named as cheapest-and-catastrophic. ATTEMPT it honestly: system package, pip, any route you can find. The Coordinator's own attempt found no binary, no apt candidate, and a failing pip source build. If it cannot be obtained, that is a DECLARED RESULT under AGENTS.md rule 5, not a failure to hide -- record the exact commands and outputs, and state plainly that 196.3662433540 and 262.3356800075 remain UNVERIFIED against real Sage.

S2 BOX-WIDENING. Scan MATZOV.cost over a grid materially wider than the optimiser's in beta, k_enum and k_fft, at 768 and 1024, and report whether anything beats the reported optimum. The Coordinator ran a 1701-point version informally and found +0.000000 bits improvement; treat that as a claim to CHECK, not a result to reproduce, and widen further than it did. If the optimum falls as the box widens, the Carrier agreement is a property of the box.

S3 NULL OBJECT. The BATCH-011 validator's DEF-7 records that the reproduction claim has no null of the right shape. Construct one and run it: something with the same shape as the matzov-vs-primal_bdd comparison but with the signal removed, and report whether the comparison still 'finds' an ordering.

S4 DECAY TEST, extended. The red team inflated N and found Kyber-512 flips at delta ~ 2.3732 bits while 768/1024 survived N x 2^16. Extend to 2^24 and 2^32 with full re-optimisation and report the flip points per parameter set. A quantity that never decays under the parameter meant to destroy it is the inventor-protocol artifact tell.

S5 report c* per attack, never transferred between attacks. EV-MLKEM-020's c* ~ 0.007 is PRIMAL's; the Coordinator wrongly transferred it to ANOM-3 (corrected in DEC-20260803-85adf8 as CE-1). Correct values c*_matzov ~ 0.0373/0.0817/0.0548. If you compute c* at all, state the memory recipe and which attack each value belongs to.

Do NOT edit tools/sage_free_estimator or anything outside write_scope. The Coordinator edited that shim mid-batch three times and the BATCH-011 validator recorded it as a defect (DEF-2); if you need a shim change, RECORD what is needed and stop rather than making it.
These are cost-model ESTIMATES, not measurements. No ML-KEM break claim, no security proof, no crypto-scale claim beyond what the estimator's own frame supports.
